original.text: ★주요사항
- 제출방법: 첨부파일 신청서 작성(지도교수 날인 포함)하여 319호 담당자 앞 제출
※내부 검토 후, 수료학점 인정이 어려운 것으로 판단될 시 수강신청 취소기한 전 대상자 SNU 공식 이메일로 개별 안내 예정
★타학과 교과목 이수 승인신청서
1) 대학원과정의 학생으로서 전기정보공학부 이외의 다른 학과(부)에서 개설한 대학원 교과목을 수료학점으로 인정받고자 하는 경우 제출.
2) 인정 가능 학점
- 공과대학, 자연과학대학(물리, 수학 등) 전기정보공학부와 유사한 과목만 신청 가능.(이와 관련없는 과목은 불인정되나, 평점평균에는 반영됨(체육 분야, 예술 분야, 사회과학 등))
- 2020년 입학자까지는 타학과 및 학사과정 교과목은 모두 합쳐 '과정별 수료학점의 1/2'까지만 수료학점으로 인정 가능.
- 2021년 입학자부터는 (과정별 수료학점 – 논문연구 이수학점) X 1/2 까지만 타학과 및 학사과정 교과목으로 인정 가능
* 단, ‘대학원 전기·정보공학부 교과목(논문연구 제외)’ 학점이 ‘타학과 및 학사과정 교과목’ 학점보다 많아야 합니다.
※예: 석사의 경우 과정별 수료학점이 24학점이므로,
대학원 논문연구 6학점 수강했으면 타학과 및 학사과정 교과목 모두 합쳐 9학점까지만 인정, 주전공 9학점 이상 이수 필수
- 참고: 링크(관련공지1), 링크(관련공지2)
3) 인정 가능 범위
- 논문제출자격시험 이수조건(주전공 6학점)으로 인정 X, 수료 시 전기정보공학부 대학원 교과목 학점으로는 인정 X.
- 단순 수료학점으로는 인정 O, 평점 평균 반영 O.
3) 참고사항
- 원칙은 당 학기 수강신청 한 과목에 대해 신청서 제출 필수이나, 이전 학기 수강한 과목에 대해 신청서 제출 누락한 경우
지도교수님 승인 하 신청서 추가 제출 가능(신청서 좌측 상단 - 사후신청이라는 문구 기재 필요)
★학사과정 교과목 이수 승인신청서(구. 학부과목 이수 승인신청서)
1) 대학원과정의 학생으로서 학사과정 교과목을 수료학점으로 인정받고자 하는 경우 제출.​
2) 인정 가능 학점
- 대학원과정 통산하여 6학점까지 인정 가능.
※예: 박사과정생이 석사 때 학사과정 교과목 6학점을 대학원 수료학점으로 인정받은 경우 → 박사 때는 학사과정 교과목을 수료학점으로 인정받을 수 없음.
- 공과대학, 자연과학대학(물리, 수학 등) 전기정보공학부와 유사한 과목만 신청 가능.(이와 관련없는 과목은 불인정되나, 평점평균에는 반영됨(체육 분야, 예술 분야, 사회과학 등))
- 2020년 입학자까지는 타학과 및 학사과정 교과목은 모두 합쳐 '과정별 수료학점의 1/2'까지만 수료학점으로 인정 가능.
- 2021년 입학자부터는 (과정별 수료학점 – 논문연구 이수학점) X 1/2 까지만 타학과 및 학사과정 교과목으로 인정 가능
* 단, ‘대학원 전기·정보공학부 교과목(논문연구 제외)’ 학점이 ‘타학과 및 학사과정 교과목’ 학점보다 많아야 합니다.

english: ★ Key Points
- Submission period: 3 Sep 2026 (Thu) ~ 17 Sep 2026 (Thu)
- How to submit: Fill in the attached application form (including the 날인 (seal or signature) of your academic advisor) and submit it to the staff member in charge in Room 319.

※ After internal review, if it is judged difficult to recognize the course as 수료학점 (credits counted toward completing your degree program), the student will be notified individually by SNU official email before the course registration cancellation deadline.
★ Application for Approval of Courses Taken in Other Departments

1) Submit this form if you are a graduate student and want a graduate course offered by a department other than the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering to be recognized as credits for completing your program.
2) Credits that can be recognized

- You may only apply for courses from the College of Engineering or the College of Natural Sciences (physics, mathematics, etc.) that are similar to Electrical and Computer Engineering courses. (Unrelated courses are not recognized, but they are still included in your grade point average (GPA) (e.g. physical education, arts, social sciences).)

- For students admitted in 2020 or earlier: courses from other departments and undergraduate courses combined can be recognized as completion credits only up to '1/2 of the completion credits required for the program'.

- For students admitted in 2021 or later: courses from other departments and undergraduate courses can be recognized only up to (completion credits required for the program – credits earned for Thesis Research) X 1/2.

* However, the number of credits from 'graduate Electrical and Computer Engineering courses (excluding Thesis Research)' must be greater than the number of credits from 'courses in other departments and undergraduate courses'.
※ Example: For a master's program, the required completion credits are 24 credits, so

if you have taken 6 credits of graduate Thesis Research, courses from other departments and undergraduate courses combined are recognized only up to 9 credits, and you must complete at least 9 credits in your major.
- Reference: link (related notice 1), link (related notice 2)
3) Scope of recognition

- NOT recognized for the 논문제출자격시험 (thesis qualifying exam) eligibility requirement (6 credits in your major); NOT recognized as credits for Electrical and Computer Engineering graduate courses at the time of program completion.
- Recognized simply as completion credits: YES; included in GPA: YES.
3) Notes
- In principle, you must submit the application form for courses you registered for in the current semester. However, if you forgot to submit the form for a course taken in a previous semester,
you may submit the form later with the approval of your academic advisor (you must write the phrase 'Late Application' (사후신청) at the top left of the form).
★ Application for Approval of Undergraduate Courses (formerly: Application for Approval of Undergraduate Course Completion)
1) Submit this form if you are a graduate student and want an undergraduate course to be recognized as credits for completing your program.
2) Credits that can be recognized
- Up to 6 credits in total can be recognized across all of your graduate programs.

※ Example: If a doctoral student already had 6 credits of undergraduate courses recognized as graduate completion credits during the master's program → undergraduate courses cannot be recognized as completion credits during the doctoral program.

- You may only apply for courses from the College of Engineering or the College of Natural Sciences (physics, mathematics, etc.) that are similar to Electrical and Computer Engineering courses. (Unrelated courses are not recognized, but they are still included in your GPA (e.g. physical education, arts, social sciences).)

- For students admitted in 2020 or earlier: courses from other departments and undergraduate courses combined can be recognized as completion credits only up to '1/2 of the completion credits required for the program'.

- For students admitted in 2021 or later: courses from other departments and undergraduate courses can be recognized only up to (completion credits required for the program – credits earned for Thesis Research) X 1/2.

* However, the number of credits from 'graduate Electrical and Computer Engineering courses (excluding Thesis Research)' must be greater than the number of credits from 'courses in other departments and undergraduate courses'.
※ Example: For a master's program, the required completion credits are 24 credits, so

if you have taken 6 credits of graduate Thesis Research, courses from other departments and undergraduate courses combined are recognized only up to 9 credits, and you must complete at least 9 credits in your major.
- Reference: link (related notice 1), link (related notice 2)
